title: KPRDSB trustees vote on tighter rules for trustee expenses
executiveSummary: Kawartha Pine Ridge District School Board trustees will vote on updating policy BA-4.9 to align trustee expense rules with provincial law.
The revised policy bans board spending on trustee association memberships and non-essential conference expenses.
The board also outlined plans to hold two regional school council meetings this year in Peterborough, Clarington, and Northumberland.
studentParentImpact: Kawartha Pine Ridge District School Board is aligning its trustee spending rules with provincial legislation, which restricts public funding for discretionary events and trustee associations. For parents involved in school councils, the board is moving to two in-person regional school council meetings during the school year to improve local engagement. Fall regional council meetings are scheduled for Northumberland on October 14, Peterborough on October 21, and Clarington on October 28, 2026. Parents can attend these regional sessions to share feedback directly with board trustees and senior leadership.
policyChanges: Trustees will vote on revising Board Policy BA-4.9 (Expenses and Reimbursements for Trustees) and its associated regulation to align with provincial Bill 101 guidelines.

title: KPRDSB Considers Rules for Classroom Video Use and Online Ads
executiveSummary: A report on the agenda suggested updates to Kawartha Pine Ridge District School Board guidelines for classroom video use.
Proposed changes aimed to align online videos with Ontario curriculum and limit advertisement content in learning materials.
The agenda also scheduled updates on principal mentorship and the Build and Soar summer trades program.
studentParentImpact: The Kawartha Pine Ridge District School Board scheduled a discussion on how videos and digital tools are used in classrooms. Following parent feedback from Clarington, board staff suggested updating guidelines to ensure online videos directly match the Ontario curriculum. The proposed updates also focus on preventing or limiting commercial advertisements during class time. While no public consultation or vote was scheduled, these potential changes aim to ensure classroom screen time is educational, age-appropriate, and free from commercial distractions for students across all grade levels.
policyChanges: Staff suggested modifying administrative regulations ES-3.3.1 (Selection, Recommendation and Reconsideration of Learning Resources) and B-7.5.1 (Social Media and Digital Communications) to align digital tools with curriculum standards and limit ads.

title: KPRDSB audit agenda covers tracking of school fundraising and activity fees
executiveSummary: An internal audit update on school-generated funds at six KPRDSB schools was listed on the agenda.
Trustees were set to vote on the proposed two-year regional internal audit plan and charter.
A vote on the 2026 external financial audit plan was also scheduled for the committee.
studentParentImpact: School-generated funds support student field trips, clubs, and special events using money raised from fees and donations. An internal audit report on six KPRDSB schools detailed recommendations to standardize financial forms, secure school safes, and improve oversight of cheques. The report also suggested using board-wide purchasing agreements for common school trips to help save families money. While these updates focus on behind-the-scenes financial controls, proper management ensures student funds are safeguarded and spent properly. The agenda did not include any public consultation or participation opportunities.
policyChanges: The committee was scheduled to vote on adopting the 2026 Regional Internal Audit Charter. No board-wide policy or administrative procedure changes were proposed on this agenda.

title: KPRDSB Agenda Featured Update on $22 Million in Summer Upgrades
executiveSummary: A summer capital project update was on the KPRDSB agenda to review 22 million dollars in school improvements across 48 sites.
An update was scheduled on targeted funding for accessibility improvements and concrete removal at Courtice Secondary School.
The agenda noted temporary washroom facilities at Bowmanville High School while universal washroom renovations wrap up.
studentParentImpact: The summer capital project update was listed on the Kawartha Pine Ridge District School Board agenda to outline completed repairs and upgrades across local schools. Most planned summer work was scheduled to wrap up before the school year started. At Bowmanville High School, students face ongoing washroom construction due to unexpected cabling delays, though temporary washrooms are set up on site. Families at Courtice Secondary School were noted for future concrete removal work planned for summer 2027. The agenda did not list any opportunities for public participation or input.
policyChanges: No policy or procedure was up for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.
